result: In a Norwegian patient-organisation survey of 828 people with CFS, pacing was rated useful by 96%, rest by 97% and shielding/quiet by 96%, similar across severity levels.
reason: Independent patient survey showing pacing among the top-rated approaches, matching the survey part of the claim; uncontrolled, non-representative sample.

result: Among 828 Norwegian CFS survey respondents, 79% of those who had graded training said it worsened their health, 57% found help challenging negative thoughts useful, and ratings were similar regardless of severity.
reason: Finding is specific to the Eckey 3,925-person survey and its severity/cluster results (this paper reports no severity effect); its strongest overlap is patient-reported worsening after graded exercise, the harms finding.

result: On polysomnography, 32 CFS patients without sleep or mood disorders had more slow-wave sleep, lower sleep efficiency and a higher microarousal index than 14 controls, with an NREM distribution unlike 30 sleep apnoea patients.
reason: Independent PSG cohort with lower sleep efficiency and more N3, the same measures and direction as the finding; replicates rather than extends.

result: In a Georgia population-based study (83 CFS, 202 insufficient-symptom, 109 well), each 1-point rise in allostatic load index raised the odds of CFS (adjusted OR 1.26, 95% CI 1.00-1.59), with a well < ISF < CFS gradient and an inverse correlation with fatigue duration (r = -0.26).
reason: Measures a composite allostatic load index, not cortisol levels; no atlas finding covers allostatic load.

result: In CFS muscle biopsies, myosin-isoform fibre typing showed a shift from slow (type I) to fast-twitch fibres, while single-fibre cross-sectional area, force, shortening velocity and calcium sensitivity were unchanged.
reason: Independent biopsy cohort showing lower type I and more fast fibre proportion, same measure and direction as the finding (sample size not given).

result: In 42 CFS patients under 40, a small heart on chest X-ray was common; echo showed a small LV chamber and poor cardiac performance in those patients, and cardiac function on repeated exams tracked symptom exacerbation and remission.
reason: Same group as the cited Miwa work, so not an independent replication; adds within-patient fluctuation of cardiac function with symptom severity.

result: On 24-h ambulatory monitoring, 38 Fukuda CFS patients had lower systolic blood pressure and abnormal diurnal BP regulation than matched controls, with a primary biliary cirrhosis fatigue comparison group.
reason: Measures ambulatory blood pressure, not heart rate or HRV; no atlas finding covers resting or ambulatory BP.

result: On 24-h ambulatory monitoring, 38 Fukuda CFS patients had lower systolic blood pressure and abnormal diurnal BP regulation than matched controls, with a primary biliary cirrhosis fatigue comparison group.
reason: No blood or red cell volume was measured; lower BP alone does not test the claim.

result: By real-time PCR of gastrointestinal biopsies, parvovirus B19 DNA was found in 40% of 48 CFS patients vs under 15% of 35 controls; HHV-7 was common in both groups and EBV/HHV-6 appeared in 15-30% of all biopsies.
reason: Tests herpesviruses and parvovirus B19, not enteroviruses; the positive signal is B19 in gut tissue.
